study_type: Human and animal observational and preclinical study
key_claims: Researchers identified specific changes in the metabolic activity of the gut microbiome that are linked to exceptional human longevity.
Amplifying this specific gut microbiome metabolic activity using engineered bacteria led to improved metabolic health in aged mice.
limitations: The source does not provide specific details on the mechanisms or exact types of bacteria involved.
Effects observed in engineered bacteria in aged mice may not directly translate to human outcomes.
No specific clinical outcomes, safety profiles, or long-term human intervention results are provided.
what_not_to_say: Do not claim that engineered bacteria have been proven to extend human lifespan.
Do not claim that specific dietary changes or commercial probiotics can currently replicate these longevity benefits.
Do not state specific numbers, statistical values, or specific institution details beyond UC San Diego.
